newsitem.title: USA: USDA sees "a little increase" in 1998 crop sowings.
newsitem.headline: USDA sees "a little increase" in 1998 crop sowings.

text.p: U.S. crop sowings would increase slightly under the new Conservation Reserve Program rules, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Wednesday, but it did not provide estimates for changes for the major crops.
"There would be a little increase in plantings for 1998 crops," chief economist Keith Collins said during a news conference. "I can't tell you which crops."
Collins also said there would be "no substantial shifts" among the major crop regions in land enrolled in the reserve.
About 10 million acres of wheat land and an equal amount of feed grain land were enrolled.
First impact of the new rules will be seen in winter wheat seedings this fall, Collins said, followed by spring-planted crops in 1998.
